project_title: Synthetic urban heat screening ranks under explicit H/E/V assumptions
research_question: Which synthetic neighbourhoods rank highest for heat screening when hazard (LST anomaly), exposure (population density proxy), and vulnerability are combined under stated weights?
study_area_label: synthetic_city_grid (teaching stand-in; not verified Multan admin units)
audience: Technical employer / research supervisor reviewing reproducibility and scientific caution

data_inventory.role: Primary screening inputs for Path A

data_inventory.licence: Teaching extract; product docs at LP DAAC MOD11A2 v061

data_inventory.source: MODIS miniature DN array (Path C logic)

method_summary: Validate protocol and row contracts; compute baseline means; build equal-weight and heat-heavy min-max H/E/V composites; emit decision card with human-review flag; separately validate MOD11A2 scale/fill logic on a miniature array.
key_results: Path A: equal-weight top neighbourhoods N2, N3 under synthetic inputs (fixture-locked).
Path B: QA filter retains 4 rows; weight sensitivity can change top rank (N2 vs N1).
Path C: miniature grid yields n_valid=6, mean ≈ 36.35 °C after scale and conversion; qa_screened=false.
limitations: No genuine Multan MODIS granule was processed in CI.
LST is not near-surface air temperature.
Synthetic exposure/vulnerability proxies are not census ground truth.
Ranks are relative prioritisation under stated weights, not calibrated health risk or expected loss.
Single 8-day composite labelling does not establish climatology, trend, or attribution.
licence_note: Repository teaching materials under project licence; NASA product use subject to current EOSDIS/LP DAAC policy.
figures_to_include: One limitations callout figure or box
environment_note: Stdlib Python 3 for fixtures; optional GDAL/pyhdf only for learner-side real HDF (outside CI).
